answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to maintain a continuous mesa of unique attestation history that is periodically synced to the network tide against a public checkpoint. An attacker creating many fakes must invest proportional ongoing compute and storage to keep every fake's history consistent and attested by peers, because any gap or duplication is slashed when the network reaches the next wharf of verifications. This raises the cost linearly with the number of identities while honest agents pay only once.
